items.title: The multiplicity of a one-dimensional module after multiplying by an element, as a sum over the height one primes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section on periodic complexes and multiplicities
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes e_R(M, 0, x) for a finite module over a Noetherian local ring with dim Supp(M) ≤ 1 and dim Supp(M/xM) ≤ 0 as the sum over the height one primes q_i of ord_{R/q_i}(x) times length_{R_{q_i}}(M_{q_i}) (statement lines 311-325). The proof is a genuine four-stage reduction: a two-out-of-three additivity argument, a comparison with the sum of the localised images, a q-adic filtration, and finally the passage to a lattice in a one-dimensional fraction field where the statement becomes a determinant computation (proof lines 329-369). The step that cannot be done by routine means is the conversion of the length of M/xM into the distance d(M, xM) and then into the order of vanishing of a determinant, which is where the numeric content of the formula sits. The claim is H2.
